strengths.I007: Cleanest evaluation of any card: an offline leave-one-brief-out fit on existing runs, run cost unchanged, with nuisance covariates (length, hedges, family match) zeroed at selection so verbosity and self-preference bias are absorbed rather than rewarded, and a principled fallback to today's BT ranking below 15 labelled briefs.
strengths.I001: Actually changes the ideas rather than reordering them: refinement effort concentrates on the ideas whose bootstrap rank interval straddles the top-3 cutoff (LUCB logic), variants are accepted only under order-swapped contests against parent and incumbent, and the independent-judge signal is something a lone self-selecting agent structurally lacks (Panickssery; Huang).

verdicts.reason: I007 can only reorder an existing finalist pool and does nothing until ~15 benchmarked briefs are labelled (with a Goodhart risk if the labels come from the eval panel), whereas I001 improves the top-3 candidates themselves at the development stage within a single run, with an on/off equal-token test and a held-out-family child-beats-parent check.

strengths.I001: Brief-agnostic: boundary-targeted critique-and-mutate cycles apply to any brief, the acceptance rule (win both orderings vs parent, one vs rank-3 incumbent) plus a 10% length cap and a different in-loop judge family limit judge-gaming, and the test is a simple equal-token on/off against uniform development.
strengths.I005: Strongest attack on judge bias in the set: objections must carry an executable artifact (sandbox PASS/FAIL or library lookup), the selector never sees critic prose, and falsified-claim rate is a measured outcome rather than an opinion.

verdicts.reason: I005's own failure analysis concedes that qualitative briefs (including briefs like this one) yield mostly not_checkable claims and s ~ 0 discriminates nothing, and its ~40%-checkable assumption is untested with 6 major critiques open, whereas I001's mechanism works on every kind of brief.

strengths.I006: Delivers a within-run gain from concrete execution feedback (Chen 2023) with a bounded 3-iteration loop, a third-family adjudicator for contested checks, and a measured outcome (falsified-claim rate under a held-out checker); templates then compound across runs, which a single agent cannot replicate.
strengths.I002: Near-zero token cost, a fixed operator taxonomy, a hand-calculated power analysis (~390 contests per arm) and a 1-of-3 uniform-random slot guarding operator diversity; conditioning edit-operator statistics on brief similarity is a genuinely non-obvious use of the idea library.

verdicts.reason: I002 by its own account may be undetectable within a few dozen runs and yields nothing until 20 training briefs have been run, while I006 produces a development-stage improvement on the first run through pass-or-strike repair against executed checks, even though both inherit a dependency on a card-0 loop.

strengths.I002: Cheapest addition here (one embedding per brief), a clear Thompson-sampling rule with stated alpha/beta and similarity threshold, and an outcome (child-beats-parent rate) that is measured rather than rated.
strengths.I007: Testable entirely offline on existing runs with no new generation, with a leave-one-brief-out AUC and log-loss that isolate the selection head, an explicit off-switch (select_by), and nuisance covariates zeroed at selection so the gain cannot come from length or family bias.

verdicts.reason: I007's effect can be isolated today with a one-time panel labelling of existing finalists and a leave-one-brief-out comparison against internal BT, whereas I002 needs I001's contest loop built first and about 50 fresh brief runs before its admittedly small effect could be detected.
